findings.detail: The three Fresha log messages (lines 204, 205, 214) and `NEED_FIELDS_MESSAGE` (line 32) are English literals, while the rest of this handler routes user-visible text through `t.common.*` from `utils/translations`. An Arabic user running a Fresha scrape sees Arabic status/completion lines interleaved with three English paragraphs, including the one that explains why add-ons are missing from the export — the explanation most likely to be read by a non-English speaker. This is the file's existing pattern (the Yalla logs at lines 67-68 are also hardcoded), so it is consistent rather than regressive, which is why it is low and not medium.
findings.summary: New user-facing log strings are hardcoded English in a bilingual tab

findings.detail: `handbooks/architecture/frontend-boundaries.md` § 'What Rex flags' lists a literal `fetch(` inside `components/**`, and line 202 contains one: `fetchFreshaVenue(freshaVenue, (u, init) => fetch(u, init))`. I am explicitly NOT treating this as a rule-2 violation. The component calls a service — the request, headers, timeout, abort and error typing all live in `services/freshaVenueService.ts` — and the lambda exists so that service can be unit-tested without a network, which is exactly the rationale rule 2 states. It also matches the identical pre-existing call at line 66 (`fetchYallaMenu(..., (u, init) => fetch(u, init))`). Recording it here so the match is visibly adjudicated rather than silently skipped.
findings.summary: `fetch` appears in a component file as the injected transport, not as I/O
